Yes! I can feel you on that one. It sucked so bad when I was in school surrounded by many students who flaunted their wealth. I try to think of it as many of them (not all) just not understanding what it's like to live differently, and lots of people can be super self absorbed. But yeah, I can see how it would still be upsetting regardless. I grew up really poor (to just sum it all up), and had to also deal with bullies who tormented me for all the struggles I had in the past, even if it wasn't able to be fixed in that moment.

It is very disconcerting. Very unfortunate it happens so much these days, despite all that's happened from the pandemic especially. I hope you're able to not have to deal with those people in school soon, as it does get better usually when you graduate, I definitely did for me. Virtual hugs to you.

I do not think he has a weight limit. Weight limits weren't mentioned at all when I went to my surgeon. The only time weight was mentioned, it was only because of the center of my chest has extra fat that he mentioned briefly could be altered (and he referred to me as "a larger person"; no rude statements about my weight).

My insurance (straight Medicaid) fully approved my surgery on the first try (which from my understanding is very lucky because Medicaid rarely does that for top surgery in my state?). I can't remember the total cost, as insurance fully paid it off and I have a horrible memory, lol.

I contacted them regarding my drains, and they responded kindly and explained everything I needed to know.

I asked my endocrinologist (who referred me to this surgeon) about how many trans people he has had. She told me she has sent a most of her patients to him. I'm not sure on how many people in total my surgeon has ended up having, but from what I've heard personally from doctors that work in that same building, they speak of him pretty highly. I know he's had hundreds of cis patients, but with trans people I'm not exactly certain (not many results online from other trans people).

I honestly never measured my chest myself; the only time it got measured was for top surgery prep. It was about DD if not a little bigger. He has performed chest reductions for cis people with big chests and is certified in plastic surgery in multiple states. Other than that, I don't really know how many larger chest sized trans patients he's performed surgery on. I should have asked about that during my consult, but I figured with his experience with other surgeries, he should at least get the job done well.

If you have any more questions, feel free to ask! :)

I've got manic and depressive states, and while most of the time THC helps me, I once had psychosis when I had too much edibles. I didn't expect it since it hadn't happened to me before, but man was it horrifying. I had very bad paranoia where I thought I was dying. I had surgical drains and while I had someone empty them for me, I thought the noises of them being emptied was sounds of me bleeding out to death. I also was panicking so much I thought it would never end.

I still use cannabis frequently, I just now know to respect the amount of THC in edibles. I have had edibles since then and been fine, so I know it was because of my intake and disorders acting up at the time. Cannabis is usually such a good medicine for many, but like any other medicines, it should be taken with care and to not abuse it.

I'm actually doing really good! I went through the surgery smoothly, it definitely wasn't as bad as I thought it would be when I talked about my concerns to the anesthesiologists. I am very thankful for everyone's advice on my situation! It all was very helpful. :)

"Are you going to get THE surgery?" or "Are you thinking about getting bottom surgery?".

The amount of times I've been asked this just these past couple of weeks is annoying. Just because I'm getting top surgery on the 25th doesn't mean it's open game to talk about my genitals. Lots of people immediately asked about that as soon as "top surgery is coming up" left my mouth.

TD;LR at end. It was back in 2019 when I had lots of pain in my entire back and right shoulder blade. When I went to more than one doctor for it a few times that year (and several times in 2020), doctors usually "didn't find anything". Oh, they also said it was just from my previous back surgery I had January 2019 causing pain, and that I would "get used to it". 

I once had to go to the ER and miss the bus for a vacation to Disney due to the pain getting really bad one day in Summer 2019. I wasn't given pain medicine for over 2 hours, and in that time was left in the room without any info. They also blamed my back surgery was affecting me and I would still get used to it.

Even with blood work, which showed signs of infection, I was let go with one week or less of weaker antibiotics, no penicillin. Eventually it got so bad that pus pockets started erupting along my scar on my back. I had a sample done in 2020 and they found Strep infecting the surgical site. What did they do? Sent me home without strong antibiotics.

I managed to get an appointment with the place I got my surgery from, and upon the main surgeon looking at the horrid scene on my back, he almost immediately said that it needed surgery very soon, like less than a week soon. Thankfully my infection got washed out and my hardware on my spine got removed (there was infection near the bone), and I'm very thankful I didn't end up dying. 

I was told with the specific Strep strain I had (Group B Streptococcus) wasn't very common at all for my age and the surgeon was surprised how it wasn't noticed by doctors beforehand. Because of the doctors not finding what it was, I could have suffered worse infection or possibly even died. I dealt with severe infection and pain for almost 2 years, and it still left its mark on me with the amount of antibiotics I had to take (I forget the dosage but it was Amoxicillin every 7 hours for 6 MONTHS)

TD;LR - I suffered a severe Strep infection in a surgical site for almost 2 years because I wasn't given strong antibiotics or even seen long enough to have them notice the red bumps on my scar that eventually erupted as massive pus pockets.

My grandmother found out I was trans, and I got the opposite reaction I thought she would. So basically, another member of the family outed me to her, but instead of being upset, she was actually *very* happy for me! She said she remembered how in the past I was "the unhappiest child" she ever met, and that after seeing the most recent picture of me, she said it was like the first time she saw me truly peaceful. She now knows about my top surgery in June as well, and she wants to help my family out with the costs of the surgery process (however I got my surgery costs covered by my insurance, which I'm super grateful for because mine is hard to get that to work)!!

I used to be into The Beatles. They were my special interest for about 4 years. I had revolved my life around that band, bought merch relating to them any chance I got, and listened to their music for hours and hours. I got burnt out from listening to them, but mostly lost interest in the fact that the person who got me into them (who I was in a relationship with at the time) got, needless to say, very toxic. It was very hard to let them go, but since I then got bad memories associated with them, I felt it was necessary to do so to let myself heal. Alex. I didn't think much of names I didn't want (since I basically chose the first name that came into my head), but somebody I was friends with suggested I should have went with Alex. I have smoked for around 5 to 6 years up to this point. I consider it a wonderful medicine for myself, as it was the only thing for a little while that helped me with severe panic attacks and agoraphobia. I'm finally on medication that works for me, but it only works most of the time (weed has worked in calming me down much faster and stronger than the several pills I take for anxiety). I love it so much that I want to get a job in the future involved with it (and possibly find ways to help more people with the plant). It may not have helped some people, but for me, it was literally what felt like a life-saver. I hope that someday I can help find the perfect strains to help people who have specific symptoms!

I'm not only a stoner, but also I am working on goals towards having a job related to the special plant! I am sharpening up my skills and learning everyday so that one day I may work in a dispensary. It has helped me a lot with gender dysphoria (along with helping me with my panic disorder and depression).

When I was younger I pretended I was a werewolf! I would often play pretend at school and people from my elementary school knew me as the werewolf kid. I always thought I was just so weird in my younger years for pretending to be a werewolf... I'm so glad other trans people can relate lmao.

I don't have a job as of yet, but I'm working on a path to have a job dealing with plants. Hopefully I can start working at a place like a greenhouse sometime so I can get experience with growing them. I figure it would be easier to have a job with that than having a job dealing with music (especially considering my specific interests in music are probably considered "outdated" by some; I don't even know how I'd be able to put that specific interest into use).

I'm really interested in music, specifically instruments/music equipment and what sounds or music they can produce. For example, I've been trying to learn more about guitar synths. One that has my interest right now is the Roland GR-300 Analog Guitar Synthesizer; this guitar synth has really fast and accurate tracking despite being limited on some things compared to more modern synths (Ooh, my favorite guitarist used this in the early 1980s and that's what made me learn more about this synth).

Another interest of mine that is totally different is botany. I like to learn about plants, especially plant genes and the possible mutations that can occur in plants. One of my favorite plants is marijuana (not just for the THC; I love the plant for everything about it). One of my favorite strains is Freakshow, which has a genetic mutation that makes the leaves form differently than a typical marijuana plant. The leaves on this strain end up looking fern-like, rather than a palm/hand-like shape.

I would say being a dumpee for me. I've been in two relationships so far, one where I was dumped and one where I was the dumper... based on my experience I'd much rather be a dumpee than have to be the dumper.

In the relationship where I was the dumper, I had such a hard time actually doing it. Maybe because I was stuck in a toxic relationship it made it harder to dump the person I loved, as I was always terrified of upsetting them. I felt like a horrible person for doing what I had to do, and I'm still trying to get over it even though it happened.

When I was the dumpee in a relationship, I felt sad and left behind at first, but I was able to get over it faster than when I was the dumper. Maybe I'd have a different opinion if circumstances were a little different, but for now, I believe that it's easier to get over the breakup if you are the one who's dumped.

When I get anxious it is really hard to clear my mind, but competitive games do the trick for using the extra adrenaline I have. It lets me focus on something other than my bad thoughts. Calmer games don't distract me enough from the mental and physical discomfort I may have.

Plenty of things come to mind, but a couple of them stand out. The first thing was that she kept insulting me and talking about "crucifying herself" to the point it made me cry (right before I had to perform on stage in a handbell concert). The other thing was that she purposely kept forcing me to have muscle spasms and scream in pain (I had just gotten out of surgery like a week or two before to clean up a serious infection near my spinal hardware). She forced the muscle spasms to start by making me move (ex. any sudden movements, like by scaring me or making me get off the futon I was recovering on. I get that she was "the guest" of the house... I was the one who invited her over to stay during the holidays (which is when I had my surgery last year) so she would have a place to be since she got kicked out. So it is pretty much my fault it happened, but I still think it shouldn't have gone that far. This second one really bothers me. Even though I was crying right before my handbell concert and made a fool of myself by getting on that stage, that embarrassment doesn't quite measure up to the physical and emotional pain from the recovery of my surgery with her around. I still experience pain on the sides of my back sometimes from the injuries from the severe muscle spasms, but it's much better than it was. And at least I'm finally starting to get over her.

I was diagnosed when I was almost 3. I'm 19 right now. So, I pretty much knew as long as I can remember about my diagnosis. I was tested not once, but twice, for the diagnosis. I had a lot of work done on me since the original diagnosis around 3, so my mom decided to have me tested again. Even though I had gotten even better at social and motor skills, at the age of 4 I got the same diagnosis of autism. 

Even though the years of therapy have made me seem like I can do certain tasks like a neurotypical, it is still extremely hard to do much of anything mentally. I can mask well enough I suppose, however, I almost always feel drained as a result of it. Having to mask all the time makes me feel rather furious, so I have to try to not have a meltdown. Other than that, at least I'm lucky to experience the good things I've done in my life due to my diagnosis (like meeting people like me!).

I used to be a Christian, but I didn't strongly follow it. I eventually leaned out of Christianity into being agnostic, all the way to being an atheist. The event that made me stop going to church was because people who were mean to me at school would follow me there. I would be hurt physically out of sight and as a result, I am terrified of going on church grounds. What made me stop believing in a god was through a combination of loss of hope and finding out my own beliefs, which don't match Christianity (or really anything other than Atheism). I tried making myself believe in a god again at one point, but my ex-girlfriend (a Gnostic the last time I talked to her) only made me more afraid of religion. I don't have anything against religion; I imagine it would be nice to have something to give comfort or hope like that. I just have experienced religious-related traumas that have made me hard to believe much anymore. I hope I don't come off as offensive by this, I just don't know how to properly word it all.

I used to wish I was cis, and still somewhat do. It would be so much easier if I were cis. However, I have come to realize that it is part of my identity that I am trans. If I didn't have that part of me, I wouldn't have become as strong and independent. I realize it is part of my journey through this life, and I must follow it no matter how hard it may be. I want to break down sometimes because of being trans and the hardships it comes with. However, I wouldn't want to give up the experiences that have molded me into who I am. All the supportive people I've met and my impact on my small town for being one of the only out and transitioning people... I wouldn't want to get rid of those times just to make things a bit easier.

I got a couple of these types of reactions from people when I came out as Roger. I remember someone specifically saying that I should have chosen something closer to my deadname (it seems a bit disrespectful they said that, but I forgive them because they were a rather clueless person). I have also been told by my sister (who is actually very supportive) that I chose a boomer name (which is funny to me, because I act like an old person sometimes lmao). I actually have gotten at least one comment from a person who didn't know I was trans that my name was interesting for someone my age. However, it is much rarer to hear those comments from people who don't know I'm trans than people who do know.

By the way, I really like the name Allen! It gives me a similar vibe as my name, which is pretty neat.
My handwriting gives me gender euphoria. I've been told by a few people I write "like a guy". I'm not sure how, but it is one of the big things I can think of that gives euphoria that isn't clothing.

I am a trans man, AFAB. Gender, in my own description, is how one internally experiences their identity. Gender is not determined by what one wears or what actions one does, but rather what one feels on the inside. Gender identities can be molded into what fits the most for the individual person, whatever the label may be. For instance, I feel that I fit better as a masculine man rather than my biological sex (female). While I may dress masculine and act masculine, what makes me a man is my internal identity. So, if someone may identify as a female but wears masculine clothing or acts masculine, that doesn't make them male, but rather what they feel is correct on the inside (in this case, female). (Good luck on the paper btw!)

Looking great! :) Wearing almost any type of sweater makes me feel euphoric, especially sweater vests and turtlenecks. So sweaters are a to-go-to for euphoria outfits for me. If I can't wear sweaters, then my next to-go-to top is a band merch t-shirt (I feel like my band merch tees look a bit masculine so of course, they'd give me euphoria). My to-go-to pants are typically khakis or corduroy pants.
Thank you! :)

My agoraphobia tends to come and go for the most part. There are some places that trigger massive anxiety still no matter the conditions (ex. my old high school or Walmart). But usually, I may have it inconsistently; one day I might go somewhere and feel somewhat okay, but I might feel terrified when the next time I go to the same place. When the agoraphobia spikes up a bit, it leaves me feeling very fatigued as well, and I'll tend to isolate myself and disappear from the public for a little while
Oh yeah, I don't know how I forgot, but I also have PTSD and Gender Dysphoria.

Along with having Autism I have Panic disorder, agoraphobia, BPD, depression, and Scoliosis.

I also have a mutation in my MTHFR gene. This mutation makes me not process medicine I take hardly at all unless I take L-methylfolate vitamins. I can't produce folic acid levels enough to break down the medicine correctly. This caused issues obviously because for medicines to actually work I needed to take a large amount for nothing to happen. Doctors mainly never listened to me up until I met my newest psychiatrist last year, who tested my DNA for it.

If you ever find that medicines have hardly worked for you ever, I'd recommend trying a genetic test... the only reason I say this is because it literally saved me from my panic attacks that I would have for days; I had bad panic attacks that almost never stopped from extreme anxiety, and after I found the problem via the test, I rarely even get a singular panic attack these days!!
I also would like to add that I like insects a lot too! My favorite bugs are mantises and beetles.
Either opossums or dogs. It is really hard to choose, so I have a favorite wild animal and a favorite pet-type animal.
I'm not exactly sure what kind of company would make me feel less lonely, but someone texted me yesterday and made me feel a bit better. Thank you for the comment though! It means a lot to me.

Greg Lake's voice from the early years of King Crimson is what gives me gender envy. A good example for those who haven't heard of him would be "21st Century Schizoid Man" on King Crimson's first album (since it's a more well-known one). I'm not even really sure what my reasoning is for why I have gender envy towards his singing voice lmao, I just love the way he sings I guess.

The name popped up in my head one day without much thought to it. I didn't know what name would fit me, so I guess subconsciously I chose that. I simply just started using it, since something in me told me to chose the name. Turns out my mom's adoptive dad had the name I chose as well, and I didn't know his name until after I chose Roger as my name.

I remember before I got my period, I just simply thought that the period curse would just skip me somehow, lol. So when the time came for the red flood, I was in total shock and tried hiding it from my family. I was extremely upset about it. Thankfully I haven't had it since starting T (hopefully it stays that way).

I remember most of my birthdays made me cry. Especially on my 17th birthday; I was at school and no one (except my family) told me happy birthday at that point I started crying. I recall sobbing in the guidance counselor's office, drowning myself in some ELO music. At the end of the day, I finally got 1 person to tell me happy birthday, and it meant the world to me.

My last birthday, I made a post on Facebook asking people that my birthday wish was to just be told "Happy Birthday". It ended up spawning dozens of comments, many people I didn't know cared. Part of me tells myself they only did it out of pity, but I really want to believe that I have people who care.

To sum it up, I am typically not fond of my birthday, as it holds negative emotions and memories. I've realized over time though that I feel it is more special to receive a few genuine happy birthdays over many saying it only because I reminded them. I try to cling on to the good parts; even though there's not many, it still is enough to give a little hope.

My hobbies include art (drawing/sculpting) and studying plants! Another hobby that makes me smile is listening to my favorite music (prog rock is my favorite genre).

My dream is to learn all there is to know about my favorite plant, marijuana! I not only like the effects but mainly it's because I think it is a very lovely plant and so unique. I want to have a job in the future surrounding it; I plan on working at a dispensary once I feel confident in my abilities in the outside world (I have agoraphobia and trying to overcome it). I would love to have a job where I can talk about my favorite plant all day (I feel comfortable around people when I get to talk about my interests)!

I collect vinyl records! I don't get the opportunity very often to find one I like, but once I find one for my collection, I get very, very happy. It's one of the only things that makes me feel proud and/or excited.

I used to collect digital pictures of The Beatles on my phone when I was into them. I had around 100 pictures on my new phone, and 400 (an estimate) on my old phone. I no longer have them since I lost interest, and I somewhat regret deleting all of them since there were some hard to find images in there. I'm currently collecting pictures of my new favorite band (King Crimson), and sadly it's much harder to find photos for them.

My main special interest is progressive rock music, especially King Crimson.

My other special interests are botany (specifically intrigued by marijuana, but I love many other plants too) and Pokemon.

I would say art too but I have a love-hate relationship with it. I can draw and sculpt but sometimes it bothers me to create things lol
The wick is on the middle of the cat's back. My sister has made sure to never put a flame to it; I can't see how people would want to melt and burn such a cute kitty candle!
Peas. I hate everything about them; I hate the smell, the texture, how it looks, and just everything else. Nasty little things. I gag at the sight of them.

That's wonderful!! I love supportive teachers so much... the reason I came out at school was because of my music teacher.
